## v2.2.3

JellyPilot 2.2.3 fixes Linux Embedded MPV startup failures caused by missing Lua support and includes the desktop playback and browsing improvements merged since 2.2.2.

### Highlights
- **Linux startup compatibility:** packaged libmpv now requires Lua support, fixing the `embedded mpv option osc failed: -5` failure reported on Fedora Wayland in [#234](https://github.com/hewel/jellypilot/issues/234). Linux packages include or declare the LuaJIT runtime dependency.
- **More Linux SDR surfaces:** Embedded MPV Playback can use compatible 8-bit UNORM presentation surfaces when 10-bit presentation is unavailable. Internal video textures remain 10-bit; HDR10 output still requires a compatible 10-bit Wayland surface. Also corrected the SDR target black level to avoid lifted blacks.
- **Playback tools:** added Jellyfin Trickplay seek previews when available, Linux MPRIS media controls, a temporary editable Viewing Queue, secondary text subtitles, and A/B repeat for the current Playback Session.
- **Browsing and TV presentation:** added profile-scoped Saved Filters, native TV presentation for living-room PCs, sticky browse/detail navigation, and improved restoration of scroll positions across view rebuilds.

### Improvements and fixes
- Added explicit play/resume controls throughout the Library Browser and independent removal Undo for Personal Lists. Watch History removal hides an item locally without changing server progress.
- Refined browsing artwork transitions, player focus, narrow controls, artwork action icons, and missing cast portraits.
- Kept global notification toasts out of active playback and retained the ordinary dark player scrim without progressive video blur.

### Platform and acceptance notes
- Linux continues to default to Embedded MPV Playback; Windows and macOS continue to default to External MPV Playback. Linux source builds now require supported Lua or LuaJIT development files.
- HDR10 remains experimental. Broader display compatibility, real playback, colors, and the new UI interactions still require human acceptance; automated checks do not establish those results.
- Windows embedded runtime DLLs remain unsigned and may be blocked by Smart App Control.
- Android development continues in the source tree, including mobile/tablet and remote-controller work, but this desktop release does not include an Android artifact.
